target.title: ci(qa): reuse Matrix live workflow for releases
target.body:
Stack 3 of 4. Depends on #103589.

## What Problem This Solves

Release checks duplicate the Matrix live-lane setup instead of calling the
maintained QA Lab live-transport workflow, while manual full Matrix proof and
release proof can drift in trust validation, retry, artifact, and status
semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make `QA-Lab - All Lanes` reusable with exact-ref validation and explicit lane
inputs, then route the release Matrix profile through that workflow and consume
its status output. Manual `matrix_profile=all` continues to fan out the five
bounded profiles so the 92-scenario proof stays within per-job timeouts.

## User Impact

Release maintainers get one Matrix live-lane implementation for focused release
proof, with deterministic mock-provider inputs and explicit status propagation.
Manual full Matrix validation keeps its parallel transport, media, and E2EE
coverage.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts`: 45/45 tests
  passed on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx5mgn8jwgz9a3skm5e2g4gn`.
- `node scripts/check-workflows.mjs`: pinned actionlint fallback, zizmor, and
  workflow interpolation guards passed on the same Testbox.
- Autoreview caught the initial loss of manual `all` fanout; the fanout was
  restored with direct contract coverage, and the fresh rerun completed clean
  with no accepted/actionable findings.
- `git diff --check` passed.

target.title: test(extensions): derive Firecrawl batch expectations from tracked tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `scripts/test-extension.mjs` tests hard-coded the Firecrawl extension as having exactly two tracked test files. That made the tooling test brittle: when Firecrawl gains or removes tests, the batch-plan assertions and exact-exclude coverage can go stale independently of the extension test planner's real inventory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `listTrackedTestFilesForRoots()` helper to derive Firecrawl's tracked test files from the same inventory source as the extension test planner. The assertions now verify the planner output against the current tracked Firecrawl tests instead of a manually maintained pair of filenames.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change. This only makes the extension test tooling coverage track Firecrawl's actual test inventory, so future Firecrawl test additions do not silently leave the batch exclude assertions under-covered.

## Evidence

Exact head: `12d74a8b5298d2b9b078d1c9615fc256e2298cfe`

Validation:

- Focused test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` -> 1 file, 44 tests passed.
- Format: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` -> passed.
- Lint: `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` -> passed.
- Whitespace: `git diff --check` -> clean.
- Types: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.json --incremental false --pretty false` -> passed.
- Autoreview: `env -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u OPENAI_ORG_ID -u OPENAI_PROJECT_ID .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` -> passed with no findings.

Scope note:

This PR previously included Firecrawl inherited-config hardening. That was removed after review because normal authored JSON/JSON5 config and include merge paths do not preserve a prototype-bearing Firecrawl config object, and the production hunk overlaps the broader own-property config PR in #103492. The current head changes only `test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` and does not change Firecrawl runtime config semantics.

target.title: fix(qa): simplify smoke lanes and isolate fanout
target.body:
Related: #101186
Related: #101187
Follows: #102256

## What Problem This Solves

#101186 restored automatic QA Smoke coverage, but its implementation coupled a hardcoded three-row Actions matrix to a second dynamic shard planner, added speculative scenario weights, pinned a scenario count that immediately drifted, and left `subagent-fanout-synthesis` in a shared concurrent suite worker.

That exact scenario failed twice on recent `main` runs while Matrix and the other Telegram shard passed:

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28935299128
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28947909491

A first two-lane version of this PR proved that one 93-scenario Crabline job exceeded eight minutes. Setup took only about 40 seconds; the runtime was the per-shard package build plus the full scenario set. This revision bounds the critical path by splitting Crabline into three equal 31-scenario shards.

The targeted scenario contracts from #101187 remain correct: Slack and WhatsApp restart/resume stay live-driver-only, and the silence-sensitive channel baseline stays isolated.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Replace the weighted planner with four explicit bounded lanes: Matrix plus three shards for the current Crabline default channel.
- Partition Crabline deterministically by sorted scenario ID, producing equal 31/31/31 shards today.
- Keep the lane IDs independent of the current Crabline default channel so that channel can change later.
- Fail closed if the smoke profile gains an unsupported third channel instead of silently adding runner fanout.
- Remove the hardcoded scenario total; profile growth is selected automatically.
- Isolate `subagent-fanout-synthesis`, which owns asynchronous child completion delivery and failed inside a shared seven-scenario worker.
- Re-enable both QA Smoke jobs after #102256's temporary action-level kill switch.

## User Impact

Automatic QA Smoke returns with four bounded Blacksmith shard jobs: 5 Matrix scenarios and three Crabline shards of 31 scenarios each. The aggregate required check remains fail-closed and artifact behavior is unchanged.

The additional runner fanout is deliberate: every shard currently pays a roughly 3.5-minute package-build floor, while a single 93-scenario Crabline lane exceeded eight minutes. Three Crabline shards should restore the critical path to roughly the prior 6-8 minute range while keeping the planner substantially simpler than #101186.

## Evidence

- Two-lane exact-head observation: Matrix passed in 4m30s; the 93-scenario Crabline job was still running beyond eight minutes before the superseding push.
- Recent #101186 runtime shape: Matrix completed in roughly 4-5 minutes; each 46/47-scenario Telegram shard completed in roughly 8-10 minutes, including duplicated package builds.
- Focused Testbox after the 31/31/31 split: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28962361871 — planner and workflow guards passed, 38 tests total.
- Earlier focused Testbox: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28960709690 — planner, catalog, suite-planning, and workflow guards passed, 104 tests total.
- Exact failing-batch replay on Testbox lease `tbx_01kx1apqv7ee0ybrjm9mxhn5k1`: 7/7 passed; logs show `subagent-fanout-synthesis` ran in a dedicated `scenarios=1 concurrency=1` worker.
- Fresh clean Testbox changed gate: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28961085005 — typecheck, lint, dependency guards, and import-cycle checks passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh autoreview after the four-shard revision: clean, no actionable findings, confidence 0.78.
